rows.what the ink shows: A tall b-like upright, a crossed t and a separate dot survive above the heavy horizontal cancellation; the opening and final low letters are covered. The complete two-word sequence cannot be recovered securely.
The left glyph has two joined bottom bowls between a tall initial downstroke and a rising right arm. Both bowls remain visible below the diagonal cancellation.
Two arms meet at a leftward vertex beside W, but the supposed lower equality bar merges with several long cancellation strokes. The surviving strokes do not securely distinguish the full relation.

A tall shaft has a small open upper hook and a lower bend entangled with the word below; the crossing strokes obscure whether the middle contained a loop. The lower-right A has two slanting legs and a crossbar, followed by B with two rounded bowls.
An opening round o and single n hump survive at the left. Only one tall loop and a terminal upright remain over the cancelled second word, whose intervening letters are hidden.

The opening e-loop joins a low n arch; the next word begins with a shallow v-like bowl and continues in low joins to a separate terminal u stroke. The final short word has a raised d peak followed by its low e exit.
The opening parenthesis is intact. The following word is covered by a broad horizontal deletion, with only a short upper curl and a small upright left above it; these do not establish the full word.

An initial loop and descending stroke survive, followed by two short upright remnants. Thick oblique cancellation strokes cover the middle and ending, so the full word is not recoverable with confidence.

A narrow initial down/up stroke is followed by two distinct medial lobes, then a separate long left-hooked descender and period. The nearby proj. has the same four-part sequence; the extra medial components distinguish proj. from op.
The inserted abbreviation has a short initial stroke, an oblique s, a small closed o, a low joined m and a separate terminal point above the insertion line.

A large initial curved stroke returns into a small loop; a later small hooked form survives near the following A. The long cancellation line merges with the intervening baseline and prevents reliable separation of On a.
A small curved left remnant and an upright nub remain, but the rest is a solid horizontal cancellation blot with a pointed right end. The n cannot be independently distinguished.
The word begins with a closed q loop and long descender; the compressed middle rises to crossed t strokes with a detached upper bar, then ends in a long low e stroke.

The initial looped d and detached i dot are visible, followed by a long low connected sequence and an angular descending turn. The separate final tall l and e are visible at the page edge, but the compressed interior does not distinguish all letters of minuer.

The beginning has a looped bend followed by a deep descending stroke; the middle is flattened into a long line, followed by a small peak, a separated dot and an upright with a low foot. These strokes do not securely separate the proposed letters of possible.

A fine upper-left hook enters a steep descending stroke, but heavy repeated ink covers most of the numeral and forms a low lateral spur. The hook supports 1 while the covered center prevents a secure reading.
Under the deletion line, c remains open at the right, a has a small low rounded turn, and the final r has an upright stem with a short raised head.
A low initial r is followed by a short accented e and curved s; the u is flattened, then l rises and t has a short rightward cross-stroke before the final small e.
The initial O retains its large open outer curve and small inner loop; n is extended along the baseline and the separate a survives as a dark small body beneath the cancellation line.

A detached upper upright stands over a separate angled lower sign with a right belly and leftward return, supporting a compact fraction but leaving its denominator uncertain. The separate following word begins with a short upright and an angular n arch; its remaining tiny rise and long flattened tail do not securely separate o-r-m-e.
